ncHmEUmJZf4.summary: Matt Kulukundis explains how Google designed SwissTable, a fast, cache-friendly hash table, step by step from std::unordered_map. The talk covers open addressing, SIMD probing and the tradeoffs of changing a fundamental data structure.
ncHmEUmJZf4.why: HN repeatedly cites it as the definitive explanation of SwissTable, the design behind Abseil, Rust's hash map and Go's maps.

np_ylvc8Zj8.summary: A feature-length documentary on how the City of London and Britain's overseas territories built a global web of offshore secrecy jurisdictions after the empire declined. It traces how this network captured and hid wealth from around the world.
np_ylvc8Zj8.why: Commenters repeatedly recommend it in tax haven and offshore finance threads as an excellent, low-budget overview of British offshore finance.

n8m7lFQ3njk.summary: Douglas Hofstadter's Stanford Presidential Lecture argues that analogy is the core of cognition, illustrating how concepts, categorization and thought arise from analogy-making.
n8m7lFQ3njk.why: HN regulars treat it as an essential, fun Hofstadter talk for any discussion of concepts, analogy and metaphor.

nm1TxQj9IsQ.summary: Andrew Huberman's podcast episode on what makes us sleepy, helps us sleep soundly and keeps us alert. It lays out the science and a set of behavioral tools such as light timing.
nm1TxQj9IsQ.why: HN users repeatedly credit it with fixing their sleep, especially its advice on morning light and dimming lights in the evening.

nJPERZDfyWc.summary: Kirby Ferguson's video essay series arguing that creativity is built on copying, transforming and combining existing work. It covers music, film and technology, then turns to copyright and patents.
nJPERZDfyWc.why: HN invokes it constantly in debates over originality, copyright and AI training, and calls it the best explanation of creativity as remixing.

nT-TGvYOBpI.summary: Dan Geer's Black Hat 2014 keynote argues that cybersecurity is a matter of power and policy rather than wishful thinking. He covers surveillance, the vulnerability market, software liability and privacy as the capacity to misrepresent yourself.
nT-TGvYOBpI.why: Cited over and over as an important talk, with commenters borrowing its ideas on cheap surveillance, offense-favoring security and liability.

nM9f0W2KD5s.summary: Peter Thiel is the first guest on Eric Weinstein's The Portal, in a nearly three-hour conversation about technological stagnation, institutional failure and the link between growth and violence. They discuss universities, the economy and the search for a more ambitious future.
nM9f0W2KD5s.why: HN people recommend it as a thought-provoking, wide-ranging case for the stagnation thesis, worth hearing even if you disagree with Thiel.

nYg6jzotiAc.summary: A restored HD upload of the 1983 BBC series Fun to Imagine, in which Richard Feynman talks informally about everyday science. Topics include jiggling atoms, fire, rubber bands, magnets, electricity, mirrors, seeing, big numbers and ways of thinking.
nYg6jzotiAc.why: HN commenters point to it as an equation-free, charming way to hear Feynman explain physics to laypeople, including his famous refusal to explain magnetism with simple analogies.

niKblgZupOc.summary: The 8-Bit Guy covers IBM's 1981 CGA graphics system, including how composite output and artifacting produced extra colors beyond the nominal palette. He argues CGA looked better in period than it does on RGB monitors.
niKblgZupOc.why: HN recommends it for showing how old developers exploited the smeary nature of composite signals and what CGA really looked like on period hardware.

nLApFANtkHs.summary: Daniel Azuma's ElixirConf 2018 talk on whether Docker and OTP conflict. He shows they can coexist and uses Horde and DeltaCrdt, with a live tank-game demo, to keep state alive across container kills.
nLApFANtkHs.why: Recommended for its practical strategy for preserving state on ephemeral containers, and for the live demo.

nfDoml-Db64.summary: BobbyBroccoli's first of three parts on Jan Hendrik Schon, the Bell Labs postdoc whose fabricated organic semiconductor results nearly won a Nobel Prize. It covers his rise and the context around Bell Labs.
nfDoml-Db64.why: HN repeatedly recommends the series as a gripping account of scientific fraud, and cites it whenever research misconduct comes up.

nYkdrAPrdcw.summary: Facebook engineers explain why they abandoned the traditional MVC paradigm for a more functional architecture, introducing Flux and React. They use the unread-message-count bug as a case study of the problems of bidirectional data flow at scale.
nYkdrAPrdcw.why: HN points to it as the original talk that explains the motivation behind React, Flux and Redux, and that sold some commenters on React.

n691pLhQBkw.summary: An excerpt of the 2005 Harvard debate in which Steven Pinker gives his prepared case on biological sex differences and the under-representation of women in science. It covers cross-cultural patterns in preferences and abilities and the overlap between male and female distributions.
n691pLhQBkw.why: Pointed to repeatedly in gender-in-tech threads, especially around the Google memo, as a science-based treatment of sex differences.

n02tImce3AE.summary: Guitarist Jim Lill methodically tests what in an electric guitar affects its tone, swapping parts on a partscaster and even trying a 2x4 body. He finds that wood and construction matter far less than people assume.
n02tImce3AE.why: Cited as a fun, experimental debunking of tonewood claims that shows electronics dominate electric guitar sound.

ne99laPUxN4.summary: Conal Elliott presents his paper on automatic differentiation, deriving a simple, generalized AD algorithm from a natural specification. Varying the representation of derivatives yields forward and reverse mode algorithms that avoid the complexity and statefulness of backpropagation.
ne99laPUxN4.why: Cited as the more accessible companion to the paper, and as the most interesting treatment of AD via compiling to categories.

nxyxcTZccsE.summary: Stanford Health Care hosts Christopher Gardner and Robert Lustig on whether all calories are equal, with a focus on processed food and sugar. The talk questions the idea that calories in versus calories out fully explains weight and health.
nxyxcTZccsE.why: HN points to Lustig's talk when arguing that processed food changes metabolism and that a simple calories in/out model is poor.

nBNTAmLRmUg.summary: Techmoan demonstrates the Tefifon, a vintage German audio player that combines elements of record and tape with a grooved elastic loop. He shows how it works and plays it.
nBNTAmLRmUg.why: HN fans use it as the gateway to the Techmoan channel and praise it as one of the most fascinating obscure audio formats.

nIoXOplUvAw.summary: Blender Guru's beginner tutorial series, in which you model, light, texture and render a donut while learning Blender's core features. This is Part 1 of the Blender 3.0 version.
nIoXOplUvAw.why: Called a rite of passage for new Blender users and the standard first recommendation for learning the program.

nUBtKNzoKZ4.summary: A clip of Louis CK on Conan riffing that everything is amazing and nobody is happy, about people complaining over airplane wifi and taking modern technology for granted.
nUBtKNzoKZ4.why: HN invokes it whenever people grumble about convenience, technology or AI that would have seemed miraculous not long ago.

nfY0lrdXar8.summary: Jacques Pepin demonstrates deboning a whole chicken, quickly and with complete control. It is a short, wordless-feeling technique demo that shows a skill most cooks never learn.
nfY0lrdXar8.why: HN calls it the single best cooking video on the internet and suggests it as a skill worth practicing for an hour.

ngpsJKQR_ZE.summary: A short anarchist-leaning video by Larken Rose arguing that the Constitution and similar documents cannot legitimately grant anyone the right to take other people's property. It uses a rhetorical 'paper that lets me rob you' setup to challenge belief in political authority.
ngpsJKQR_ZE.why: Libertarian-minded commenters post it in surveillance, government and constitution threads as a red-pill argument that political authority is illusory.

nmgFG7PUHfo.summary: Veritasium tells the story of the Fast Fourier Transform, from its use in detecting nuclear tests to Cold War politics, and how it could have changed the arms race. It includes a short, intuitive explanation of what the Fourier transform does.
nmgFG7PUHfo.why: HN points people to it as the explanation that finally made Fourier transforms and the FFT click, with a good historical story.

nnR8fDW3Ilo.summary: Festo's promo video of SmartBird, an ultralight bionic flying model inspired by the herring gull that flaps and twists its wings to fly. It shows the robot in flight.
nnR8fDW3Ilo.why: Recommended as a spectacular example of bio-inspired robotics, and a pointer to Festo's other work.

nphxoUxSvgY.summary: Alexander Rose of the Long Now Foundation describes the design and construction of the 10,000 year clock conceived by Danny Hillis. He covers the project's history, methods, and how different cultures built things to last millennia.
nphxoUxSvgY.why: Recommended in threads about long-lasting structures and passing knowledge across generations, as a long but fascinating talk.

nsaUX48t0w8.summary: A short demo of a walking droplet on a vibrating silicone oil bath passing through a double slit and producing interference, a macro-scale analogue of pilot-wave behavior.
nsaUX48t0w8.why: HN users share it to build intuition about wave-particle duality and pilot-wave ideas in quantum mechanics threads.

nvK8fua6O64.summary: MrBtongue argues that modern theme-park MMOs lost what made earlier sandbox online games compelling, and that MMOs could be saved by returning to sandbox design.
nvK8fua6O64.why: Commenters call it one of the best, most insightful explanations of sandbox versus theme-park MMO design.

n1QEj09Pe6k.summary: Wendover Productions explains why modern airliners fly no faster than they did decades ago, covering the economics of speed and fuel efficiency, and why supersonic travel faded.
n1QEj09Pe6k.why: Recommended as a clear economic explanation of aviation tradeoffs, relevant to Concorde and supersonic startup threads.

n3Xv_g3g-mA.summary: Kurzgesagt explains why humans feel loneliness, its evolutionary role, and how modern life can turn it into a harmful downward spiral. It cites research and offers ideas on what to do about it.
n3Xv_g3g-mA.why: Shared in loneliness threads as a well-sourced, empathetic explanation, including for people struggling with it.

n8Dd5aVXLCc.summary: Alexander Nix of Cambridge Analytica presents at the 2016 Concordia Summit on using big data, psychographic profiling and behavioral microtargeting in elections.
n8Dd5aVXLCc.why: HN points to it as the company's own pitch, used in debates about data-driven manipulation and extrapolated to today's AI.

nAbCKa0FzjQ.summary: Matt Godbolt, creator of Compiler Explorer, tours surprising optimizations modern compilers perform, such as turning loops into closed-form sums and using popcount instructions. He explores what the compiler does behind the scenes.
nAbCKa0FzjQ.why: HN recommends it as a detailed, entertaining look at the crazy optimizations compilers do.

nLF0n9SACd4.summary: Dan Abramov's JSConf Iceland talk on what came after React 16, with live-coded prototypes of async rendering and time slicing. It previews the ideas that became concurrent mode and suspense.
nLF0n9SACd4.why: Recommended as the clearest demo of what concurrent rendering solves, including the memorable clock animation.

nQpxAvjD_30.summary: A Ryan George comedy sketch about the absurdities of shopping on Amazon, including nonsense brand names, fake reviews and scammy sellers.
nQpxAvjD_30.why: HN recommends it as a funny sketch that lays bare the crazy things people have gotten used to on Amazon.

nU8DcBF-qo4.summary: Peter Norvig's 2007 Google talk on theorizing from data, covering what huge datasets can do for language understanding, translation, information extraction and inference. It argues that more data often beats cleverer models.
nU8DcBF-qo4.why: HN recommends it as the clear explanation of why Google's statistical, data-first approach works.

nXaxk27zwlk.summary: Chandler Carruth walks through tuning C++ performance, from writing benchmarks to analyzing results on real CPUs and compilers. It focuses on small-scale problems such as loop kernels, data structures and algorithms, and on keeping compilers from optimizing benchmarks away.
nXaxk27zwlk.why: HN recommends it as an eye-opening primer on benchmarking and performance analysis, especially for people who have not benchmarked on Linux.

n068fel-W9I.summary: A special lecture from MIT's Private Pilot Ground School in which Lt. Col. Randy Gordon, a fighter and test pilot, describes F-22 flight controls. Topics include thrust vectoring, the pilot command system and how software handles failures.
n068fel-W9I.why: Recommended as a fascinating insider account of how the F-22's software makes it easier to fly than a Cessna.

nIKhUizkXxA.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science builds and operates a simple mass spectrometer, using it to measure potassium isotopes in a salt substitute. He explains the design choices and the theory behind it.
nIKhUizkXxA.why: Recommended as an expert-made DIY build that explains why the apparatus is designed as it is, though one commenter notes a missing baseline run.

nJslrTT-Yhc.summary: Adam Something gives a short, sarcastic argument that carbon capture does not live up to its promises. He says the energy it uses would be better spent replacing fossil sources directly.
nJslrTT-Yhc.why: HN commenters cite it to argue carbon capture is a distraction from stopping emissions at the source.

ncPyMUfNyVM.summary: A two-minute clip of Andreas Antonopoulos explaining why a 51% attack on Bitcoin would not destroy it and what such an attack would cost. It is a succinct take on mining security.
ncPyMUfNyVM.why: HN commenters link it as a short, favorite explanation of Bitcoin's security and the sustainability of a 51% attack.

noQcWra6sbU.summary: Netanel Rubin's 31C3 talk chains Perl's syntax quirks into a powerful remote code execution attack, taking down popular Perl-based projects.
noQcWra6sbU.why: Recommended as a funny, engaging look at how Perl's quirks create real security vulnerabilities.

nsJZ_kKjXcE.summary: Lock-picking YouTuber Bill Johnson (BosnianBill) explains how to choose a high-security lock and why, showing examples and comparing designs. It covers what makes some padlocks more pick-resistant than others.
nsJZ_kKjXcE.why: HN users recommend it as an amusing, practical overview of padlocks from cheap to high security.

n28W4AmvMDE.summary: A long Huberman Lab podcast episode with Dr. Robert Lustig on the calories-in, calories-out model and how sugar, fructose, fiber and processed foods affect insulin, liver and metabolic health.
n28W4AmvMDE.why: HN mentions it mostly as a source for the argument that sugar is toxic, though some commenters push back on claims like fructose being addictive.

nSKp2StlS6s.summary: Dylan Beattie's parody of 'You Give Love a Bad Name' about hypermedia APIs and REST, performed with his band at developer conferences.
nSKp2StlS6s.why: Shared as developer humor, with commenters insisting any Dylan Beattie mention must come with this song.

ne6tB2KiZuk.summary: Bobby McFerrin uses audience participation at a World Science Festival event to demonstrate how instinctively people follow the pentatonic scale.
ne6tB2KiZuk.why: HN shares it as a delightful demo of the pentatonic scale's near-universal appeal and of a crowd syncing without instruction.

nBiJB8YuDBQ.summary: A John Stossel special arguing that Americans can be criminalized for almost anything, with examples of overzealous prosecutors and regulators such as the EPA. It is a documentary on overcriminalization.
nBiJB8YuDBQ.why: HN recommends it in discussions of overcriminalization and prosecutorial overreach, notably after Aaron Swartz's death.

nLjFTHTgEVU.summary: A Google Ventures talk on how unconscious biases shape product decisions, hiring and workplace interactions. It draws on research, including work by Google scientists, on how to counter them.
nLjFTHTgEVU.why: HN recommends it as an interesting look at the psychology research behind bias in hiring and performance reviews.

nO5vjmDFZaI.summary: Jason Scott's multi-episode documentary on the bulletin board system scene of the 1980s and 1990s, built from over 200 interviews. It captures how hobbyists ran dial-up systems before the internet went mainstream.
nO5vjmDFZaI.why: HN recommends it as a definitive, nostalgic history of BBS culture whenever people ask what the pre-internet online world was like.

nQHBAdShgYI.summary: CGP Grey asks whether Star Trek-style teleportation would kill you and recreate a copy, working through the philosophy of identity and the Ship of Theseus. It is a short animated explainer.
nQHBAdShgYI.why: Pointed to in threads about mind uploading and teleportation as a good, accessible look at personal identity.

nTFEUsudhfs.summary: Salman Khan explains why he created Khan Academy, a structured library of video lessons with interactive exercises. He calls on teachers to flip the classroom, with lectures watched at home and homework done in class with teacher help.
nTFEUsudhfs.why: HN recommends it as an inspiring pitch for video-based, flipped-classroom learning.

nbiVbd_CEIA.summary: ArtosisTV's commentary on Game 1 of DeepMind's AlphaStar (Protoss) against top Zerg player Serral at Blizzcon 2019. Artosis analyzes the match with beginner-friendly commentary.
nbiVbd_CEIA.why: Cited as footage of AlphaStar beating a top human StarCraft 2 player, and for accessible game analysis.

nkRxvEjprBM.summary: A clip from the film The Lives of Others showing Wiesler as a ruthless, efficient Stasi interrogator who uses a recorded interrogation to train new officers. HN uses other scenes from the same film as well.
nkRxvEjprBM.why: HN cites it, and the scent-sample scene in the film, in threads about surveillance and Stasi methods such as smell registers.

nnl6nY8YKHs.summary: An interview with Nick Bostrom at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute presenting his simulation argument: at least one of three propositions about posthuman civilizations and ancestor simulations must be true.
nnl6nY8YKHs.why: Offered as a less technical introduction to Bostrom's simulation paper.

nq_SpRBXRmE.summary: The Pruitt-Igoe sequence from Koyaanisqatsi set to Philip Glass's 1998 re-recorded score, showing the housing project's demolition.
nq_SpRBXRmE.why: HN mentions it as a favorite documentary scene and as a reference for the Pruitt-Igoe demolition.

nv7-YM4wno8.summary: Spencer Lisenby explains dynamic soaring, a technique that lets unpowered radio-controlled gliders reach speeds above 835 kph. He covers the physics and the design, build and flying challenges.
nv7-YM4wno8.why: Recommended as a detailed, wonderful explanation of the physics of dynamic soaring and record-speed RC gliders.

nxeMoaxUpWk.summary: Scott Manley surveys the research on whether people can adapt to rotating artificial gravity, from early Soviet centrifuge tests to modern studies. He concludes it is an engineering problem and discusses Coriolis effects and station radius.
nxeMoaxUpWk.why: Linked as the clear explainer on rotational gravity and its Coriolis oddities.

n63XXHY4A7I.summary: A five-minute lightning talk from React.js Conf 2016 by Elie Rotenberg on protecting the DOM from tampering. It shows how React tree obfuscation (react-armor) can shuffle class names, tags and tree structure to defeat CSS-selector-based ad blocking.
n63XXHY4A7I.why: Cited as the origin of react-armor style DOM obfuscation, and as a favourite short talk from the conference.

nJff23UdNAI.summary: Dan Callahan presents Mozilla Persona, a decentralized, cross-browser authentication system that removes site passwords, at PyCon 2013. He explains how the protocol works and how to add it to a Python site.
nJff23UdNAI.why: HN cites it as the best explanation of how Persona's provisioning and login work, and of why it used email addresses as identity.

nXCSloXZ-wc.summary: Tom Dale explains the internals of the Glimmer VM, Ember's rendering engine, which compiles templates to opcodes. The talk includes a performance benchmark demo.
nXCSloXZ-wc.why: HN points to it for understanding Glimmer and Ember's view layer, and as a reference for opcode-compiled templates.

njVv7J2azY8.summary: Ang Cui and Jonathan Voris present firmware modification attacks on networked printers at 28c3, showing how HP printers can be compromised and used as footholds for malware inside sensitive networks.
njVv7J2azY8.why: Recommended as a jaw-dropping demonstration of how insecure embedded printer firmware is.

nqzpAbK9qFk.summary: John Carmack's roughly 90-minute keynote at Oculus Connect 2014, covering mobile VR and the Gear VR work, followed by audience questions.
nqzpAbK9qFk.why: Cited as an example of Carmack's fluent long-form speaking and as an informative talk on VR.

n-AbPav5E5M.summary: A sped-up two-minute view of morning rush hour at a busy Utrecht junction, where thousands of bicycles and buses pass each day. It illustrates a city where about a third of trips are by bike.
n-AbPav5E5M.why: HN links it as a vivid example of what bike-centred cities look like in debates on cars, helmets and urban design.

n-BZ5-Q48lE.summary: aGameScout explains rolling, the third major NES Tetris playstyle, in which players tap the back of the controller to move pieces faster than hypertapping. It covers how the technique works and where it comes from.
n-BZ5-Q48lE.why: HN points to it as the concise explanation of the latest competitive NES Tetris technique.

n4M7e79XTYk.summary: Spaceballs' 9 Fingers, an Amiga demoscene demo released at The Party in 1993, recaptured here in 50fps HD. It is the follow-up to their demo State of the Art.
n4M7e79XTYk.why: HN cites it as a mind-blowing example of 1990s demoscene technique on Amiga hardware.

n6h7fL22WCE.summary: Reason TV profiles Elvis Summers, a Los Angeles musician who crowdfunded dozens of tiny homes for homeless people. City officials moved to remove them while pushing a multibillion-dollar housing plan.
n6h7fL22WCE.why: Cited in homelessness threads as an example of a private effort to build cheap shelter that LA shut down over code violations.

nAGHUkby2Is.summary: Alan Watson Featherstone, founder of Trees for Life, describes nearly 30 years of work restoring the ancient Caledonian Forest in the Scottish Highlands, illustrated with his photography.
nAGHUkby2Is.why: Cited in ecology threads as background on how overgrazing prevents Scottish forests from regenerating.

nAsrsMPftOI.summary: Tom Scott follows the ISO 3103 / BS 6008 standard to make an international standard cup of tea, using specialist tasting equipment. The video shows how precisely the standard is specified.
nAsrsMPftOI.why: Used to illustrate that the standard targets consistency rather than taste, and to discuss what standardization is for.

nBaIRm4610o.summary: Dr. John Campbell reviews a mouse study on accidental intravenous injection of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine and its potential to cause myopericarditis. He walks through the methods and findings and discusses the aspiration technique.
nBaIRm4610o.why: HN uses it in vaccine-safety threads as a source on aspiration and the consequences of inadvertent intravenous injection, with mixed enthusiasm.

nCgQDjiotG0.summary: Google's 2010 Chrome ad filmed web page rendering with a high-speed camera, comparing it with a potato gun, a pirate ship and lightning. It presented browser speed as Chrome's key selling point.
nCgQDjiotG0.why: HN cites it as an example of Chrome's speed-focused marketing and of how fast Chrome seemed at launch compared with other browsers.

nLv_INgaLq8.summary: An episode of C++ Weekly in which Jason Turner shows modern C++14 compiling to the Commodore 64's 6502. It demonstrates writing efficient high-level code for 8-bit hardware.
nLv_INgaLq8.why: Cited as an example of using modern C++ on 8-bit hardware.

nNMNglk_CvE.summary: A Rocky Mountain IPv6 Taskforce talk in which T-Mobile's Stephan Lagerholm explains how the carrier went IPv6-only using DNS64 and 464XLAT, with a live Android demo and best practices.
nNMNglk_CvE.why: It is the standard citation in IPv6 threads that large mobile carriers already run phones with only IPv6 addresses.

nWTvXbQHwWs.summary: Lex Fridman's long interview with Chris Lattner, creator of LLVM and Swift, covering the future of computing and programming languages. It touches on compilers, hardware, and his work at Apple, Tesla, Google and SiFive.
nWTvXbQHwWs.why: Mentioned as an interesting Lattner conversation whenever Swift, LLVM or language design come up.

n_6p-1J551Y.summary: A demo of the Cubli, a 15 cm cube that uses reaction wheels to jump up onto a corner, balance there and fall in a controlled way to move. The video shows these three abilities chained into locomotion.
n_6p-1J551Y.why: Brought up whenever reaction wheels or self-balancing cubes come up, with the jump-up maneuver singled out as the coolest part.

naleynXS7yo.summary: A Key & Peele sketch in which two friends keep misreading the tone of each other's text messages while making plans.
naleynXS7yo.why: HN brings it up in threads about tone getting lost in text-based communication.

nfRouGH0oMg.summary: A short clip from an ACM and Computer History Museum interview in which Leslie Lamport discusses writing his paper on time, clocks and the ordering of events. He explains its link to special relativity.
nfRouGH0oMg.why: HN cites it as a primary source for Lamport's relativity inspiration behind logical clocks in distributed systems threads.

nmC0ygr08tE.summary: A short MIT Math Lab video showing millimetric droplets bouncing and walking across a vibrating fluid bath, guided by their own pilot waves. These droplets show diffraction, tunneling and quantized orbits, which were once thought to belong only to quantum systems.
nmC0ygr08tE.why: Cited in pilot-wave theory threads as a vivid visualization of how quantum-like behavior can arise in a classical system.

nnsSUqgkDwU.summary: Google's 2009 'Search Stories' ad, shown in the Super Bowl, tells the story of an American who falls in love in Paris entirely through search queries.
nnsSUqgkDwU.why: HN cites it as a model of emotional product storytelling and as inspiration for visualizing one's own search history as a narrative.

nqFVOL7mLd4.summary: A short clip about the Australian Collins class submarine HMAS Rankin reportedly defeating US Navy ships in a war-game exercise.
nqFVOL7mLd4.why: Cited in discussions of how quiet diesel-electric submarines can evade detection by large navies.

nsjDnYxJ0bo.summary: Jack Gallant's lab demonstrates reconstructing movie trailer clips a subject watched from fMRI brain activity, using regression models trained on hours of viewing data. The video shows the original clip beside the reconstruction.
nsjDnYxJ0bo.why: HN cites it as the landmark brain-decoding demo and compares newer reconstruction work against it.

nuruzFqMgIw.summary: Karsten Nohl and Jakob Lell present BadUSB at Black Hat 2014, showing that USB controller firmware can be reprogrammed to impersonate other device types. They demonstrate system compromise and a self-replicating USB threat that current defenses cannot detect.
nuruzFqMgIw.why: HN uses it as the standard reference for why USB devices are dangerous beyond ordinary viruses.

nybVFJVXbww.summary: Dr Mike Pound explains the suspected backdoor in the Dual_EC_DRBG random number generator and how elliptic curve constants could let someone predict its output.
nybVFJVXbww.why: HN points to it as an intuitive explanation of how NIST standardized a backdoored generator.

nzCaZQqAs9I.summary: Wim Hof guides viewers step by step through his breathing method, with some explanation of the science he cites behind it. It stresses learning from the source and avoiding unsafe settings.
nzCaZQqAs9I.why: Mentioned as the source for how to do Wim Hof breathing, for example as a sleep or relaxation suggestion.

n-FMpNBfna8.summary: Home video of the 11 March 2011 Japan earthquake, filmed as an early warning system detected the P wave and gave seconds of notice before the shaking began. The raw footage shows the warning in action.
n-FMpNBfna8.why: HN cites it as a concrete real-world example of how much warning earthquake early-warning systems can provide.

n0CT8zrw6lw.summary: A short Atlantic documentary on Cleveland's 1986 Balloonfest, when 1.5 million balloons were released at once and the attempt went badly wrong.
n0CT8zrw6lw.why: Cited as a shorthand for a spectacularly misguided publicity stunt, or as a classic embarrassing Cleveland episode.

n5QRgpjfarY.summary: A short clip from the Diablo Immortal announcement at BlizzCon 2018 in which a Blizzard representative asks the booing audience if they do not have phones.
n5QRgpjfarY.why: Cited as a shorthand example of a tone-deaf corporate response, especially around Blizzard and mobile gaming.

n7ZyJw_cHJY.summary: A short clip based on Zbigniew Brzezinski's views about the erosion of national sovereignty and his criticism of the war on terror. It is titled Political awakening.
n7ZyJw_cHJY.why: HN commenters link it, mostly without comment, in threads about surveillance, security policy and loss of privacy.

nFZGpES-St8.summary: Karen Sandler, then Executive Director of the GNOME Foundation, talks at OSCON 2011 about the risks of proprietary, closed-source software in implanted medical devices like her own pacemaker-defibrillator.
nFZGpES-St8.why: Brought up whenever medical device security or open-source firmware in implants is discussed.

nHaTRWRj8G0.summary: A one-minute clip from the 1995 Steve Jobs interview in which he describes what he saw at Xerox PARC and what he missed. He says he grasped the graphical interface but not the networking and object-oriented parts.
nHaTRWRj8G0.why: HN cites it as Jobs's own account of what Apple took from Xerox and why Xerox failed.

n_sNclEgQZQ.summary: On The Ben & Marc Show, Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz compare Trump and Biden policies on tech, crypto, AI and startup taxes, framed around their 'Little Tech Agenda'. They also discuss the Trump assassination attempt.
n_sNclEgQZQ.why: HN cites it as the source for how Andreessen and Horowitz explain their political shift toward the Republicans.

nfHuZ5qrYX4.summary: A one-minute clip of Windows Phone 7 and Bing product placement from an episode of Hawaii Five-0, in which a character says 'Bing it!' and another checks a Windows phone.
nfHuZ5qrYX4.why: Cited mockingly as an example of awkward, cringe-inducing product placement and ad culture.

nifUBDgPhl4.summary: A performance of Bach's Coffee Cantata (BWV 211) conducted by Ton Koopman, with English subtitles. It is a comic secular cantata about a father and his coffee-loving daughter.
nifUBDgPhl4.why: Shared as a fun example that Bach wrote secular, humorous music, usually in coffee threads.

nkuOuxRD1Bc.summary: Ali G pitches his ice cream glove idea to marketing professionals and even talks to Donald Trump. It is a comedy sketch of a clueless entrepreneur seeking investment.
nkuOuxRD1Bc.why: HN uses it as a joke reference whenever a startup pitch or market-sizing claim sounds naive or absurd.

nn2FB1P_Mn8.summary: The classic IT Crowd scene in which tech support answers every call with 'Have you tried turning it off and on again?'
